en: The root ملك (mlk) primarily means to possess or own something, often with exclusive rights and the ability to exercise authority over it.
The root مَثَلٌ (mathal) signifies a description through comparison, often used for important or remarkable states.
The root "mwt" primarily means "to die," the opposite of living.
The root MWL primarily refers to "wealth" or "property." It encompasses anything one owns, from currency to animals like camels, which were a significant part o

The root مكر (mkr) primarily means to practice deceit, guile, or circumvention, often with the intent to harm clandestinely.
The root م ل أ primarily means "to fill." It can describe filling a vessel, satisfying the eye with beauty, or being filled with emotions like fright.
The root مرأ (mrA) is primarily linked to the word مَرْءٌ (marʾun), which means 'a man' or 'a human being.

The root مَدَنَ (madana) relates to dwelling in a city or being urbanized. A "madīnah" is a city.
The root مسك (msk) primarily means to hold, retain, or withhold. It can refer to grasping something firmly, restraining someone, or abstaining from an action.
In the Quran, منن prominently concerns favor, bestowal, grace, and reminding others of a favor.
The root مَرَض (marad) primarily means physical illness or sickness. Tropically, it refers to spiritual or mental ailments like doubt, hypocrisy, weakness of be
The root م-ش-ي primarily means to walk or go on foot. It can also imply proceeding, journeying, or moving forward in a general sense.

The root مكن (mkn) means to establish, settle, or assign a place to someone. It also signifies giving someone mastery, dominion, or power over something, enabli

The root منع (mnE) means to be prevented, to refrain voluntarily, or to be inaccessible. It implies resistance, refusal, or something being impossible.

The root "m-t-r" primarily refers to rain.
In the Quran, مائة means one hundred. The Quranic occurrences of this lexical item are numerical and should not be defined by unrelated water-drawing senses.
The root ملو primarily signifies filling something completely, to the brim, or to its full capacity. It can also denote a period of time, like a full lifetime,
The root مكث (mkth) means to tarry, stay, or wait. It implies patience and expectation, often in a specific place. It can also mean to loiter or pause.
The root "mwj" primarily describes the tumultuous, agitated motion of the sea and its waves.
The root مَرَجَ (maraja) primarily means to send animals to pasture freely. It also signifies mixing things, like two seas that meet but don't fully blend.
The root مقت (mqt) signifies intense hatred, often due to a foul deed. It describes being an object of extreme dislike or detestation.
The root "mhl" (أمهل) means to act gently or leisurely towards someone, granting them delay or respite. It implies giving someone time to do something, like say

The root مضي primarily signifies passing, going forth, or proceeding. It can refer to time passing, or a person or thing moving onward and away.
The root "myd" primarily describes motion, agitation, or swaying, like the earth shaking or a branch bending. It also refers to a feeling of giddiness or nausea
